items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: since I met Allison and them, things began to change

ctx.x: I guess, uh, you've found it kind of difficult. Your popularity's been kind of like a rollercoaster. You've real... Had a lot of, uh, big records in the early 50s and late 40s, and I guess did fairly well in the 50s, and then in the 60s... In the 60s, uh, New Orleans music seems to have taken a really bad turn, and now it seems to be coming back a little bit more interesting.

Well, I was so busy trying to find people that was honest enough to work with, and, uh, I wasn't even keeping up with what the record was doing, because, uh, uh, to my satisfaction, I wasn't getting anything from them, so, to me, it wasn't doing anything, you know? But, uh, around the 70s is where I really adored myself in the music field, because, uh, since I met Allison and them, things began to change, you know? I saw some varied coming, and so this interested me more, of keeping up with where the songs were…

Were any of the producers back in the 40s and 50s, uh, honest, or any of them good, or were they all... I said Allison. I mean, any of the old, any of the ones from... I said maybe Allison Casper. Just Allison. I don't even want to call the rest of those people the names. Uh, that brings me to another question. One of my favorite songs that you've done is not on an album, uh, an album and such, except it can be found on an English anthology, and that's, uh, your song, Bald Head. Bald Head. How come that's not on…
